original.name: limit_function_type_contract.md
original.content:
---
description: p-limit's declared limitFunction takes a PromiseLike-returning fn and returns a Promise-returning fn with clearQueue
type: project
---
In the p-limit package, `index.d.ts` declares the `limitFunction` public contract as `export function limitFunction<Arguments extends unknown[], ReturnType>(function_: (...arguments_: Arguments) => PromiseLike<ReturnType>, options: Options): ((...arguments_: Arguments) => Promise<ReturnType>) & Pick<LimitFunction, 'clearQueue'>;`. This is a type-level contract grounded in the declarations, not a runtime restriction: the input must be PromiseLike-returning, unlike the `LimitFunction` call signature whose parameter accepts `PromiseLike<ReturnType> | ReturnType`; `index.test-d.ts` asserts the narrower limitFunction input with `expectError(limitFunction((_a: string) => 'x', {concurrency: 1}));`. The declared return type still exposes only `clearQueue` from `LimitFunction`; a later tsd verification reported `Property onIdle does not exist on type ((x: number) => Promise<number>) & Pick<LimitFunction, "clearQueue">`. The `index.js` implementation has diverged from this declared surface: the wrapper now uses `Object.defineProperties` to define both `clearQueue` (as `limit.clearQueue`) and an `onIdle` method delegating to `limit.onIdle()`, replacing the earlier `Object.defineProperty(limitedFunction, 'clearQueue', ...)`. The user asked to remember this inspected limitFunction input/output type contract for future maintenance.

In the p-limit package, `index.d.ts` declares the `limitFunction` public contract as `export function limitFunction<Arguments extends unknown[], ReturnType>(function_: (...arguments_: Arguments) => PromiseLike<ReturnType>, options: Options): ((...arguments_: Arguments) => Promise<ReturnType>) & Pick<LimitFunction, 'clearQueue'>;`. This is a type-level contract grounded in the declarations, not a runtime restriction: the `limitFunction` parameter accepts only `PromiseLike<ReturnType>`, while the `LimitFunction` call signature's parameter accepts `PromiseLike<ReturnType> | ReturnType`. The declared return type exposes only `clearQueue` from `LimitFunction`. The `index.js` implementation builds this by creating its own limiter and returning `(...arguments_) => limit(() => function_(...arguments_))` with `clearQueue` defined as `limit.clearQueue`.
